text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says Finland would jeopardise the credibility of its economic policy if it were to opt out of European economic and monetary union, EMU.

- MPs representing the governing parties criticised the government's plans regarding the parliamentary procedure for a decision on joining EMU. Some called on the government to introduce the issue as a bill to parliament.
- Women's share of HIV-positive cases in Finland has risen to about half of all cases, while the total number has remained stable in recent years.
- Finnish rapid reaction force crossed Finnish-Norwegian border to join Nordic NATO Partership for Peace exercises.
- In the first quarter of this year, foreign investors bought more than 21 billion markka worth of Finnish shares, raising total foreign shareholdings to about 130 billion markka.
- Big exhibition of Andy Warhol's art planned for the August-September Helsinki festival.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish forestry firms were among the most profitable in the Nordic region in the first quarter, but were they also more indebted than their Nordic competitors.
- Bank of Finland moving to keep banks from telling about its open market operations.
- World Economic Forum ranks Finland three notches lower on competitiveness ranking list, now 19th versus 16th last year.
AAMULEHTI
- National Board of Taxation chief Jukka Tammi held press conference to declare his innocence after police questioned him about suspected involvement in tax fraud.
- Rauma CEO Heikki Hakala says company's new owners, following a share offering by UPM-Kymmene, include various pension and mutual funds from Scandinavia, Europe and the United States.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finnet regional telephone firms join bidding for Turku local telephone company Turun Puhelin. National operator Telecom Finland has upped its offer for the company to 589 million markka.
- Finnish forestry groups raised mill utilisation rates by about 10 percent in the first quarter.
DEMARI
- Labour Minister Liisa Jaakonsaari said she would be ready to support building more nuclear power capacity if it proves crucial to economic growth and jobs.
